title: India Urges Citizens to Postpone Iran Travel as US-Iran War Enters Eighth Night of Strikes
excerpt: India's embassy in Tehran issued an urgent advisory as two US service members were killed in Jordan, 15,000 Indian seafarers remain stranded near the Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf airspace disruptions widen.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • India advises citizens to postpone travel to Iran amid escalating US-Iran conflict.
  • Two US service members killed in Jordan, marking the first military deaths since March.
  • Over 15,000 Indian seafarers stranded near the Strait of Hormuz due to shipping restrictions.
  • EU Aviation Safety Agency warns airlines to avoid Gulf airspace until at least July 29.
  • India's embassy in Tehran has urged Indian nationals to postpone non-essential travel to Iran and asked those already there to consider leaving.
  • Two US service members were killed by Iranian fire in Jordan — the first American military deaths since March — prompting an eighth consecutive night of US strikes on Iran.
  • India has ordered all shipping companies to stop deploying Indian seafarers on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz; over 15,000 remain stranded west of the strait.
  • The EU Aviation Safety Agency has advised airlines to avoid airspace over Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE, and the Gulf of Oman until at least July 29.

India Issues Urgent Advisory

India asked its nationals to postpone non-essential travel to Iran and urged those already in the country to consider leaving, as the security situation in the region deteriorated sharply over the weekend. The advisory from India's embassy in Tehran cited the "rise in instability" following escalating military exchanges between the US and Iran.

The travel alert comes on top of an earlier order by India's Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA) directing shipping companies, ship managers, and recruitment agencies to stop deploying Indian seafarers on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz "until further orders."

India is the world's third-largest supplier of seafarers, with over 300,000 sailors working across global shipping fleets. Two Indian seafarers have been killed in attacks on vessels in the region in recent days, and New Delhi lodged a strong protest with Iran, summoning its deputy ambassador over one of the deaths.

More than 15,000 Indian seafarers remain stranded on the western side of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Manoj Yadav, general secretary of the Forward Seamen's Union of India.

Two Americans Killed as Strikes Intensify

The US announced on Sunday that two American service members were killed in Jordan by Iranian fire — the first US military deaths from Iranian attacks since March. A third service member is missing in action. US Central Command said the fatalities occurred while personnel were preparing for Iranian ballistic missile and drone attacks.

President Trump ordered an eighth consecutive night of strikes on Iran in response. Central Command confirmed the latest airstrikes, launched at 6 PM EDT Saturday, targeted Iranian military coastal surveillance and air defense facilities, designed to "further degrade Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz."

Iranian state media reported explosions near Sirik in southern Iran and near Shadegan, close to the Iraqi border. An explosion was also reported in Abadan, in Iran's southwest.

"No deployment of Indian seafarers on vessels undertaking voyages involving passage through the Strait of Hormuz until further orders."

— Directorate General of Maritime Administration, India

Gulf Airspace Disruptions Widen

The military escalation has created ripple effects across the travel sector. The European Union Aviation Safety Agency strengthened its Conflict Zone Information Bulletin, advising airlines to avoid flying over Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE, and the Gulf of Oman until at least July 29. The advisory also covers airspace over Iran, Iraq, and Lebanon.

Kuwait Airways suspended airport movements after Iranian attacks damaged a power-generation and desalination facility. Bahrain reported intercepting Iranian aerial attacks. Iran has launched missile and drone strikes against American military facilities in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan while also hitting Saudi infrastructure.

The US State Department issued a worldwide travel caution urging Americans — especially those in the Middle East — to exercise increased caution, keep a low profile, and avoid locations associated with the United States.

What NRIs Should Know

For the estimated 9 million Indians living and working in Gulf countries, the escalation poses immediate safety and travel concerns. Flight cancellations, airspace closures, and rerouted flights are disrupting travel between India and key Gulf hubs including Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Kuwait City, and Doha.

Indians with travel plans involving Gulf transit should check with airlines for schedule changes, prepare for delays, and register with the nearest Indian embassy or consulate. The DGMA has directed seafarers and vessels to contact the DG Communication Centre or the Indian Navy's Information Fusion Centre for emergency assistance.
